newsitem.title: UK: West African crude firmer as Sept overhang clears.
newsitem.headline: West African crude firmer as Sept overhang clears.

text.p: West African spot crudes edged higher on Thursday, underpinned by active trade this week which has cleared out much of a prompt overhang of September barrels, traders said.
Nigerian Bonny Light loading in September fetched Dated Brent +42 cents this week but October barrels traded at +45 cents and sellers were looking to improve on those levels.
Firm price indications were hard to find on Thursday ahead of the release Friday or early next week of October contract prices by the Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC).
"Nobody wants to confirm numbers at the moment but (Bonny Light) sellers are asking nearer Dated plus 50 cents now," said a trader for a European refiner.
September barrels of Nigerian Qua Iboe also traded three or four times this week but one of the cargoes could reappear on the market, traders said.
An Oct 10-11 Qua Iboe was sold to a U.S. refiner.
"There's been the usual amount of October trade this week and September activity has picked up although there is still a fair amount available," said a trader.
Much of the remaining overhang was in the hands of refiners who could take the cargoes into their own systems should they become too distressed, traders said.
Gabonese Rabi was identified as the weakest grade with at least three September cargoes still potentially for sale.
"A lot of Rabi usually goes to the U.S. but the Brent-WTI arbitrage hasn't been too attractive recently," said a trader.
The spread between NYMEX crude and IPE Brent has shed nearly 50 cents since the start of September as Brent crude prices soared $3 a barrel on the back of heightened tension in the Middle East.
Other September cargoes still on offer included a Nigerian Forcados, which gained a couple of cents to Dated Brent +40/+45 cents and a Sept 20-22 Escravos.
Angolan Cabinda was also busy with a Sept 27-28 stem sold to a U.S. refiner for about Dated Brent -95 cents a barrel and a first decade October cargo placed into Zaire.
